data.review_body:
This has been the worst shopping experience I have ever had with Temu.
For more than 35 days, I have been suffering because of this order. I paid for my purchase and waited patiently, but I never received any SMS or phone call from the delivery company informing me that my package had arrived at the pickup point, even though this notification was provided for my previous orders.
When I discovered the problem, I repeatedly contacted Temu Customer Service. I opened an official support ticket, explained my issue in detail, and provided all the required information. However, all I received were generic, repetitive responses and promises that my case would be reviewed, without any real solution.
Every time I was told to wait, I ended up receiving the same repeated response again. I lost my time, my peace of mind, and my money, yet I received no compensation for the inconvenience or for a problem that was not caused by me.
I believe Temu did not handle my complaint seriously and failed to take responsibility for investigating the delivery issue or resolving my case fairly. This experience has completely destroyed my trust in the platform.
If my case is not resolved fairly, I will share my full experience on social media and consumer review platforms so that others can make informed decisions before purchasing from Temu. I will also pursue every available option to recover my money through my payment provider and any other appropriate channels.
I am not asking for special treatment. I am simply asking for the rights of a customer who paid for an order, waited more than a month, and was met with delays, repetitive responses, and empty promises instead of real solutions.
data.review_headline: The worst experience. I advise you to download another app for shopping; it's better than Timo. Timo is the worst app.

data.review_body:
Buyer beware: Temu's "rewards" are a bait-and-switch
Temu lures you in with promises of cash, credits, or vouchers — but the payout is always just out of reach. Every time you get close to redeeming a reward, the app asks for another purchase, another referral, another step. It's an endless loop designed to keep you spending, not to actually reward you.
This isn't just my own experience — several state attorneys general (Arizona, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Nebraska, Texas) have filed lawsuits alleging Temu uses exactly this kind of bait-and-switch scheme to lure users in with prizes that never arrive. The FTC has also taken enforcement action over Temu's gamified shopping tactics. Save yourself the frustration — don't count on ever cashing out.
